data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A hybrid protocol combining epoch-locked workspaces with a two-phase seal witness\u2014comprising a durable intent-to-seal record followed by a finalization record\u2014prevents the spurious displacement observed in lease protocols by ensuring the reclaimer must observe both the absence of intent and the confirmation of death before reclamation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Intent records can leak (not cleaned up after finalize), causing false negatives in reclamation and resource exhaustion.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Epoch counters advance despite holder death due to a faulty lease coordinator, permitting concurrent intent and reclamation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The two-phase record itself introduces a window where the holder has crashed after intent but before finalize, creating the same ambiguity the protocol seeks to eliminate.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When approaching completion, the holder writes a durable intent record containing (problem-id, proposed-content-hash, holder-epoch) to a replicated intent store. After terminal flush of evidence to durable storage, it writes a finalize record. The reclaimer must verify: (a) no un-finalized intent record exists for the problem-id, and (b) the holder's epoch lease is expired and not renewed. The required durable record is therefore the ordered pair (intent, finalize) in a holder-local but replicated store, with exactly-once semantics enforced by epoch monotonicity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
